Four of the five anchors, and all three with finite floors, are TPAGB (phase 5). MIST does not model circumstellar dust around thermally-pulsing AGB stars, and its synthetic photometry for that phase is the least trustworthy part of the grid. Real dusty AGB stars are FAINTER in the optical than a dust-free atmosphere predicts, so a grid BC is itself likely to be an optimistic bound. Obtaining the .iso.cmd fixes the grey-treatment flaw but does NOT retire this one - it must be carried as a separate stated uncertainty.

m_nuc = 19 currently has no band. A per-band repricing changes BOTH sides of the contrast: the source gains BC_X and the nucleus must be given its own band magnitude. Holding m_nuc = 19 fixed across bands (as the prompt's Stage C specifies, correctly labelled a selection convention) is not a physical statement - an old elliptical nucleus is itself red, so its g-band magnitude is fainter than its i-band one, which partly offsets the source's BC penalty. The net band dependence of the census is therefore SMALLER than BC_X alone implies, and its sign cannot be fixed without a nuclear SED. Any Stage C run under the fixed-m_nuc convention must state this, or it will read as a band-dependence result when it is a source-only result.
